Interactive prototype: tap the app buttons and watch the panel. The panel slides on its own and follows your pointer, while the phone stays fixed. Values are demo data.

Three numbers that matter

Everyone on the floor sees the same figures, in large red LED digits readable from a distance.

Employees

Current headcount on site, adjusted with a single tap on + or -.

Days without accident

A running counter that restarts the moment an accident is declared.

Days without customer complaint

A running counter for quality, reset when a customer complaint is logged.

How it works

No technician needed to change what the panel shows.

Update

A supervisor opens the app and taps +, -, Accident or Réclamation client.

Process

The control system built with SG Automatisme receives the change and recalculates the counters.

Display

The LED panel refreshes so every employee sees the current figures.

Mobile software design

Before any code was written, the app was modelled with UML diagrams so that every user action was defined in advance.

Needs the app must meet

  • Connectivity between the smartphone and the panel
  • Works on different smartphones
  • Real-time control
  • Daily automatic increment of days without accident and without reclamation
  • Reset of either counter when an accident or reclamation is declared
  • Increment and decrement of the employee number
  • Care for the human-machine interface and the display aesthetics

Mobile software result

A single, simple screen built in Android Studio with Java.

Embedded software and hardware design

An ESP32 receives the commands and drives the LED panel through MAX7219 shift registers.

IoT architecture

  • Connectivity: peer to peer (P2P) over Wi-Fi
  • Platform: mobile phone
  • Processing unit: ESP32
  • Intermediate: MAX7219 shift registers
  • Actuator: LED matrix panel
  • Sensors: none

Simulation and final product

Each part was simulated before moving on, then everything was assembled into the real panel.

Realization method

Tools: ISIS Proteus, Arduino IDE (MaxMatrix, WiFi and webServer libraries), Android Studio and Java.

  • 1. Split the project into small tasks: display, mobile app, connectivity
  • 2. Develop each task and test it on the simulator
  • 3. If it works, move on. If not, troubleshoot and repair
  • 4. When everything works in simulation, build the real product
